findings.sourceExample: Friends can sort out the same plan in a few messages.
findings.decisionEvidence: The existing editorial decision explicitly calls 'sort out the same plan' awkward without a competing-plan context and says to teach transferable 'sort out X', for example 'sort out the details of a shared plan'.
findings.issue: The draft instead freezes the awkward full source wording as the lesson title and target, and repeats 'sorted out the same plan' through the assessed items and both model answers. It teaches a bespoke noun phrase as if it were the fixed phrasal verb, contrary to its own source decision and ordinary usage.
findings.recommendedRepair: Keep the exact source sentence as provenance, but re-lemma to a bounded natural 'sort out a/the/shared plan' or 'sort out the details of a shared plan' target that still detects the source. Rewrite target-bearing assessed items naturally, with agreement on one plan supplied as context rather than fixed expression; align Traditional Chinese and recalculate spans/glossary. If this cannot be done without an overbroad owner, hold the source for editorial review.
